28.text: Then a description of a contest between the two shamans is given. Kukuˊlpɪn

29.text: vanquished the shaman from Teˊpqän. “Says that shaman, ‘Let us at least

30.text: be companions in wives.’ — ‘Agreed!’ — ‘Where shall we go first? To

31.text: you? Where is your house?’ — ‘In the village Teˊpqän.’ — ‘How long does

32.text: it take you to fly there?’ — ‘About half a day.’ — ‘Aha! my house is nearer;

33.text: better let us go there. My two wives are at home. Let us race. The one

34.text: who arrives first shall sleep with both.’” Kukuˊlpɪn is again the winner,

35.text: arriving before his rival. After supper the latter is allowed to sleep with the

36.text: older wife, Kukuˊlpɪn himself sleeping with the younger one. The visitor is

37.text: dissatisfied with the arrangement, but submits after several fruitless attempts

38.text: to exchange sleeping-rooms with the host. Then both shamans fly to the
